html:
On 6 December 1992 a crowd of Hindu nationalist volunteers tore down the Babri Masjid, a sixteenth century mosque in Ayodhya, north India. Riots followed across the country and killed about 2,000 people.

The mosque was built in 1528 or so under Babur, the first Mughal emperor. Many Hindus believe the site is the birthplace of the god Rama and that a temple once stood there. A legal dispute over it had run since the nineteenth century. In the 1980s the Vishva Hindu Parishad and the Bharatiya Janata Party made a temple at Ayodhya their cause, and L. K. Advani toured north India in a chariot in 1990 to rally support.

At a rally on the site, the crowd broke through and levelled the building in hours while police watched. The riots that followed in Bombay led to the 1993 Bombay bombings. In 2019 the Supreme Court gave the land to a Hindu trust, and the Ram Mandir opened there in 2024. The demolition marks the rise of Hindu nationalism in Indian politics.
sum: On 6 December 1992 a crowd of Hindu nationalist volunteers tore down the Babri Masjid, a sixteenth century mosque in Ayodhya, north India. Riots followed across the country and killed about 2,000 people.
